docs.text: QuestLab JSON Documentation This document describes the JSON structure for QuestLab scenario data. QuestLab scenarios are designed to allow the creation of interactive experiences revolving around the usage of media, including audio, images, text, spritemaps, and video. Scenarios can be scripted via an end-user app, but on the backend the QuestLab API outputs the scenario data as a JSON string. The Phaser frontend reads the JSON, and executes the scenario as scripted. Examples of scenario JSON strings are included in this documentation. docs.text: Actions An event consists of actions, and actions describe what happens when the user interacts with a scene. Actions are executed in sequential order, and actions from different events can be run simultaneously. Primary Attributes Parameter Type Default Description id int action id event_id int The event id the action is associated with. type string The type of action. Different actions may require different attributes to be present, and these are listed separately below. sequence int The order the action executes in the event. blocking bool true If true, this action must complete before the next action in the sequence executes. If false, the next action will execute immediately after this action executes. This is used in situations where two or more actions must occur simultaneously, such as an audio and text action to show a character speaking with subtitles. media_id int An id for a media object defined at the project level, in the assets. Not all action types require media. Audio Play an audio (MP3) file. Parameter Type Default Description volume decimal 1.0 Volume range from 0.0 to 1.0. repeat bool false If true, play the audio file on an infinite loop once it reaches the end, until a jump or cancel action stops the file. persist bool false If true, do not stop playing the audio file after a jump action. Audio actions are the only action types that can persist across scenes. Cancel Cancel an action that’s currently executing. Parameter Type Default Description action_id int An action id of a currently-running action. Actions do not necessarily need to be from the same event sequence in a scene to be cancelled, but they do need to be from the same scene (with the exception of persistent audio). Image Fixed Display an image (JPEG or PNG) file in a fixed position on the scene. Parameter Type Default Description position_x decimal The X coordinate for the image. position_y decimal The Y coordinate for the image. scale_x decimal 1.0 scale_y decimal 1.0 duration int Image Overlay Display an image (JPEG or PNG) file. Parameter Type Default Description alignment string center center A positioning for the image when it pops up. scale_x decimal 1.0 scale_y decimal 1.0 duration int Image Alignment The image alignment is used when the image is fixed, and will pop up at a certain position on the screen according to the chart below. Value Description top left top center center left center center bottom left bottom center Infobox Open an informational box. Parameter Type Default Description content string The text to show in the box (HTML allowed). call_to_actions json null A list of buttons, each containing (1) a string, and (2) an action that is performed when clicked or tapped. Jump Load another scene, ending all actions in the current scene (except persistent audio). Parameter Type Default Description scene_id int The scene id to jump to. Repeat Repeat the actions for the event, starting with the first action. If there are any actions after a repeat action, they will never execute, unless the repeat is conditional. Run Event Execute an indirect event. Parameter Type Default Description event_id int The event id to execute. Spritemap Display and animate a spritemap (JPEG or PNG) file (PNG recommended). Spritemap attributes follow a standard format regardless of whether they occur in an action, hotspot, or other data structure in the JSON specification. See the Spritemap specification for more details. Text Overlay Display a text string on the screen, overlaying everything else. Parameter Type Default Description text string The text to display (256-character limit). alignment string center center A positioning for the text when it pops up. text_font_size int 24 Size for the font, defined in pixel height. text_font_color string white Color for the font. text_font_style string Style for the font (leave blank, or “italic”). duration int The number of milliseconds the text displays before disappearing. If “0” the text displays indefinitely, until a jump or cancel action removes it. Text Alignment The text alignment is used when the text is fixed, and will pop up at a certain position on the screen according to the chart below. Value Description top left top center center left center center bottom left bottom center Translate A translation is the movement or alteration of the object in an image, video, or spritemap action, or a hotspot label. Attributes can be overridden as well. A “targetId” must be specified, or this action will be bypassed. Also, the original action must still be running, or this action will be bypassed. (Under revision.) Parameter Type Default Description target_id int An action id of a currently-running action. Actions do not necessarily need to be from the same event sequence in a scene to be translated. Image Translation (Under revision.) Video Translation (Under revision.) Variable Set or modify a global variable. Parameter Type Default Description name string A global variable that has been defined at the project level. Only dynamic variables by a variable action. operator string One of six data manipulation operators to perform on the variable: set, +, -, *, /, % operand multiple A number (integer or decimal), or a string, for which the variable is manipulated according to the operator. Operator Value Description set Assign the variable to the value specified in operand. + Add the numeric variable by the value specified in operand. If the operand is non-numeric, this does nothing. - Subtract the numeric variable by the value specified in operand. If the operand is non-numeric, this does nothing. * Multiply the numeric variable by the value specified in operand. If the operand is non-numeric, this does nothing. / Divide the numeric variable by the value specified in operand. if the operand is non-numeric, this does nothing. % Modulo the numeric variable by the value specified in operand. if the operand is non-numeric, this does nothing. random Generate a random number between 1 and 1000000000 and assign it to the variable. To narrow the results, follow it up with another variable action, using modulus (%). For example, to get a number between 1 and 20, generate the random number, then apply “% 20” to it. Video Play a video (MP4) file. Currently under revision. Wait Waits a specified amount of time before proceeding with the next action. Parameter Type Default Description duration int The number of milliseconds to wait. If 0 or less, the wait action is bypassed.

docs.text: HTTP API contract The player, the editor and the game server depend on a small set of endpoints. Two things implement the player's and the game server's: the Laravel API in apps/api (production), and the game server's file backend (development and previews), which serves the public endpoints itself from JSON files so the game runs without Laravel. Anything that honours this contract can be swapped in. Public endpoints (called by the browser) All responses are JSON. Authenticated requests send Authorization: Bearer <token> . POST /api/auth/login Body { "email": "...", "password": "..." } . Returns { "token": "...", "user": User } , or 422 with { "message": "..." } . POST /api/auth/guest Body { "name": "..." } . Returns { "token": "...", "user": User } with role guest . The Laravel API only offers this when QuestLab_ALLOW_GUESTS=true . A guest token is accepted by the game server only for scenarios with require_login: false . POST /api/auth/logout Ends the token it is called with, so signing out works everywhere that token was kept. The game and the editor call it from their "Sign out" buttons and then forget the token. GET /api/auth/providers { "google": true, "guest": true } : which optional ways of signing in this installation offers. The sign-in screens show a Google button when google is true. Signing in with Google Google sign-in is on when GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID and GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET are set. It is a redirect flow, not a JSON call: The sign-in screen sends the browser to GET /api/auth/google/redirect?return=/editor/ . return is a path on this site to come back to; anything else is replaced with / . Google asks the person and sends the browser to GET /api/auth/google/callback (register this address with Google: https://your-host/api/auth/google/callback . It is built from APP_URL ). The API finds the account by Google's id for it, or joins an existing account with the same verified address, or creates a new one. It issues a token and answers with a small page that stores the token where the game and the editor look for it ( localStorage["qbl.token"] ) and goes to return . The token is never put in an address. If nobody is signed in, the browser is sent to return with the reason after the # : #signin=cancelled , domain (the address is not at an accepted domain), unverified , expired or failed . New accounts are students. QuestLab_GOOGLE_DOMAINS limits who may sign in to those domains; accounts at QuestLab_GOOGLE_TEACHER_DOMAINS start as teachers. An account that has only ever signed in with Google has no password. GET /api/me Returns { "user": User } or 401. GET /api/scenarios/{code}/play {code} is the scenario's unique 16-letter code, the same one players have in their address bar ( /{code} ). A shortname is accepted too. Returns { "scenario": Scenario } : the published scenario document with the caller's save data in scenario.session (null if none). Returns 401 when the scenario has require_login: true (or is private) and there is no valid token, and 404 for an unknown or unpublished scenario. ?group= names the instance being joined ( public if absent, a12 for an assignment, t7 for a team; see Classes, missions and teams ). The save returned is the caller's save in that instance. 403 if the caller does not belong to it, or if the scenario is private and was not assigned to them. The document's avatars ( avatar_media_ids , avatar_portraits and their images in assets ) are the platform's, added as the document is served. Missions and avatars All need a token. Endpoint Body Returns GET /api/missions { "missions": [Mission] } : every public scenario, and everything assigned to the caller (assigned first, soonest due first) GET /api/avatars { "avatars": [{ media_id, name, image_url, portrait_url, sheet }], "avatar_media_id": 900004 or null } PUT /api/me/avatar { "avatar_media_id": 900004 } The same. 422 if it is not one of the platform's avatars { "id": 1, "code": "starshipexplorer", "title": "Starship Explorer", "subtitle": null, "description": "...", "image": "/scenario-assets/starship/backgrounds/bridge.png", "visibility": "public", "kind": "assigned", "group": "t7", "assignment_id": 12, "teacher": "Ms Tan", "team": "Comets", "due_at": "2026-12-01 15:00:00", "note": "Read chapter 4 first", "started_at": null } kind is public or assigned . A player opens a mission at /{code}?group={group} . image is the background of the scenario's first scene. Times are UTC. started_at is when the caller's save in that instance was last written, or null. The fields from assignment_id to note are only on assigned missions. Classes (teachers and admins) Under /api/teach ; 403 for anyone else. Endpoint Body Returns GET /students { "students": [{ id, name, email }] } POST /students { "email": "..." } 201 { "student": {...} } . 404 if nobody has signed in with that address DELETE /students/{id} 204. The student also leaves this teacher's assignments GET /scenarios { "scenarios": [...] } : published scenarios the caller can assign (public ones and their own; all of them for an admin) GET /assignments { "assignments": [Assignment] } POST /assignments { "scenario_id", "student_ids": [], "due_at"?, "note"?, "teams"?: [{ "name", "student_ids": [] }] } 201 { "assignment": Assignment } PUT /assignments/{id} Any of due_at , note , student_ids , teams (give a team's id to keep its instance) { "assignment": Assignment } DELETE /assignments/{id} 204 An Assignment is { id, scenario, due_at, note, group, students: [{ id, name, email, team_id }], teams: [{ id, name, group, student_ids }] } . Stars, XP and the marketplace All need a token except GET /api/shop . Guests are answered 403: stars and XP need an account. Endpoint Body Returns GET /api/me/progress { "progress": Progress } GET /api/shop?scenario={code} { "items": ShopItem[], "progress": Progress or null } : the platform's items plus that scenario's own POST /api/shop/{item}/buy { "scenario": "{code}" } { "progress": Progress } . 422 without enough stars, 409 if already owned, 404 if the item is not sold in that scenario POST /api/shop/{item}/equip { "equipped": true } { "progress": Progress } . Putting something on takes off what was in its place { "stars": 56, "xp": 240, "rank": "Explorer", "next_rank_xp": 300, "owned": [1, 102], "equipped": [102] } ShopItem is described under Stars, XP and the marketplace . There is no public endpoint that gives stars: awards come only through the game server (below). User { "id": 12, "name": "Ada", "role": "student", "avatar_media_id": 103 } role is one of student , teacher , admin , guest . avatar_media_id is optional. Internal endpoints (called by the game server) Under /api/internal , authenticated with the header X-QuestLab-Service-Key , which must equal the API's QuestLab_SERVICE_KEY . These must not be reachable from the internet; in the provided Docker setup Apache answers 404 for /api/internal on its public port, and the game server reaches those routes through a second Apache port that exists only on the Docker network. Endpoint Body Returns POST /auth/verify { "token": "..." } { "user": User } , or 401 if the token is not valid GET /scenarios/{code} { "scenario": Scenario } (no session), or 404. A shortname is accepted too GET /scenarios/{id}/access/{userId}?group= { "allowed": true } if the player may join that instance: asked before a player is let into a room GET /scenarios/{id}/sessions/{userId}?group= { "session": Session or null } : the player's save in that instance ( public if no group is given) PUT /scenarios/{id}/sessions/{userId}?group= { "session": Session } 204 GET /scenarios/{id}/instances/{group} { "instance": InstanceData or null } PUT /scenarios/{id}/instances/{group} { "instance": InstanceData } 204 POST /scenarios/{id}/awards { "user_id": 12, "action_id": 72090 } Progress plus delta_stars , delta_xp , note , rank_up . The action must be an award in the published document; a once-only award already given changes nothing. 403 for a guest GET /users/{id}/look { "look": "1,102" } : the ids of what the player has on, for other players to see Session and InstanceData are described on the Save data page. Editor endpoints (called by the editor) Under /api/editor , with Authorization: Bearer <token> . Only the Laravel API implements these (and the development stand-in, apps/api/dev/server.php , which runs the same classes). Who May admin edit every scenario teacher edit their own scenarios, and shared samples that have no owner anyone else nothing: 403 A scenario the caller may not edit answers 404, the same as one that does not exist. Errors are { "message": "..." } with 401, 403, 404, 409 or 422. A scenario is stored as rows of these tables: media , variables , items , characters , scenes , events , actions , conditions , labels . The columns are the attributes on the corresponding docs pages; attributes that only some rows have are kept in a JSON column ( params for actions, labels and media; settings for items, characters and the scenario; layout for a scene's walkable areas, spawn points and placements). ScenarioStore::SCHEMA is the authoritative list. Endpoint Body Returns GET /scenarios { "scenarios": [...] } : id, code, title, subtitle, owner, published_at , updated_at POST /scenarios { "title": "..." } 201 { "scenario": row } . The scenario gets its code and a first scene GET /scenarios/{id} { "scenario": row, "media": [...], "variables": [...], ..., "labels": [...] } : every row of the scenario PATCH /scenarios/{id} columns to change { "scenario": row } DELETE /scenarios/{id} 204. Removes its rows, players' saves and uploaded files POST /scenarios/{id}/rows/{table} columns 201 { "row": row } PATCH /scenarios/{id}/rows/{table}/{rowId} columns to change { "row": row } DELETE /scenarios/{id}/rows/{table}/{rowId} 204. Also removes what only existed because of it: a scene's events, an event's actions, labels and conditions POST /scenarios/{id}/media/upload multipart, field file 201 { "row": media row } GET /scenarios/{id}/preview { "scenario": Scenario } : the JSON generated from the rows as they are now, published or not POST /scenarios/{id}/publish { "scenario": row } . Generates the JSON and makes it what players get POST /scenarios with "template": "starship" { "title", "template" } 201: the new scenario starts as a copy of the starship hub instead of one empty scene POST /scenarios/{id}/duplicate { "title"? } 201 { "scenario" } : a copy as a new draft of the caller's. Allowed for a scenario the caller can edit, and for anyone's published public scenario (copied as published) GET /scenarios/{id}/export The scenario as a ZIP file ( scenario.json , assets/ , README.txt ) POST /scenarios/import multipart file (a ZIP), title ? 201 { "scenario" } : a new draft made from the ZIP. 422 if it is not a ZIP, has no scenario.json , or carries a file that is not a picture, sound or video. See Backups, copies and the starship hub Rules the API enforces whatever the editor sends: A row can only be created in, moved to, or made to refer to things in the same scenario ( scene_id , event_id , media_id , ...). Enumerated columns only take their documented values (action type , event kind , media type , condition operator , ...). A condition belongs to exactly one of an event, an action, an item or a character. Variable names are letters, digits and underscores, and may not start with QuestLab . Uploads are identified by their content. Images (PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF), audio (MP3, WAV, OGG) and video (MP4, WebM) up to 25 MB are accepted; SVG is not. A scenario's code cannot be changed. The editor runs the shared validator ( validateScenario from @qbl/shared ) on the preview before it publishes and refuses to publish a document with errors. The API does not repeat that check, so a client other than the editor should run npm run validate on what it builds; the game server validates every document it loads either way. Testing a draft The game plays a draft when opened as /?preview={scenario id}&scene={scene id} . It fetches GET /api/editor/scenarios/{id}/preview with the editor's token, checks the document, and plays it alone (no game server, nothing saved), starting in the given scene. This is what the editor's "Test this scene" button opens.

docs.text: Under /api/editor , with Authorization: Bearer <token> . Only the Laravel API implements these (and the development stand-in, apps/api/dev/server.php , which runs the same classes). Who May admin edit every scenario teacher edit their own scenarios, and shared samples that have no owner anyone else nothing: 403 A scenario the caller may not edit answers 404, the same as one that does not exist. Errors are { "message": "..." } with 401, 403, 404, 409 or 422. A scenario is stored as rows of these tables: media , variables , items , characters , scenes , events , actions , conditions , labels . The columns are the attributes on the corresponding docs pages; attributes that only some rows have are kept in a JSON column ( params for actions, labels and media; settings for items, characters and the scenario; layout for a scene's walkable areas, spawn points and placements). ScenarioStore::SCHEMA is the authoritative list. Endpoint Body Returns GET /scenarios { "scenarios": [...] } : id, code, title, subtitle, owner, published_at , updated_at POST /scenarios { "title": "..." } 201 { "scenario": row } . The scenario gets its code and a first scene GET /scenarios/{id} { "scenario": row, "media": [...], "variables": [...], ..., "labels": [...] } : every row of the scenario PATCH /scenarios/{id} columns to change { "scenario": row } DELETE /scenarios/{id} 204. Removes its rows, players' saves and uploaded files POST /scenarios/{id}/rows/{table} columns 201 { "row": row } PATCH /scenarios/{id}/rows/{table}/{rowId} columns to change { "row": row } DELETE /scenarios/{id}/rows/{table}/{rowId} 204. Also removes what only existed because of it: a scene's events, an event's actions, labels and conditions POST /scenarios/{id}/media/upload multipart, field file 201 { "row": media row } GET /scenarios/{id}/preview { "scenario": Scenario } : the JSON generated from the rows as they are now, published or not POST /scenarios/{id}/publish { "scenario": row } . Generates the JSON and makes it what players get POST /scenarios with "template": "starship" { "title", "template" } 201: the new scenario starts as a copy of the starship hub instead of one empty scene POST /scenarios/{id}/duplicate { "title"? } 201 { "scenario" } : a copy as a new draft of the caller's. Allowed for a scenario the caller can edit, and for anyone's published public scenario (copied as published) GET /scenarios/{id}/export The scenario as a ZIP file ( scenario.json , assets/ , README.txt ) POST /scenarios/import multipart file (a ZIP), title ? 201 { "scenario" } : a new draft made from the ZIP. 422 if it is not a ZIP, has no scenario.json , or carries a file that is not a picture, sound or video. See Backups, copies and the starship hub Rules the API enforces whatever the editor sends: A row can only be created in, moved to, or made to refer to things in the same scenario ( scene_id , event_id , media_id , ...). Enumerated columns only take their documented values (action type , event kind , media type , condition operator , ...). A condition belongs to exactly one of an event, an action, an item or a character. Variable names are letters, digits and underscores, and may not start with QuestLab . Uploads are identified by their content. Images (PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF), audio (MP3, WAV, OGG) and video (MP4, WebM) up to 25 MB are accepted; SVG is not. A scenario's code cannot be changed. The editor runs the shared validator ( validateScenario from @qbl/shared ) on the preview before it publishes and refuses to publish a document with errors. The API does not repeat that check, so a client other than the editor should run npm run validate on what it builds; the game server validates every document it loads either way.

docs.text: Architecture browser | apache (port 80, published) / | | | \ game files /media /editor /api/* /game (WebSocket) and /{code} uploaded | | | from the app files editor: app: Laravel colyseus container's (volume) static files (PHP-FPM) | public/ volume | | /api/internal via apache:8081 db <------------+ (Docker network only) Docker runs six containers: app (Laravel and the built Phaser frontend), db (MariaDB), colyseus , editor , docs (this documentation, built with MkDocs and served at /docs ) and apache . The Phaser build is copied into Laravel's public/ directory; Apache serves those files from a shared volume and forwards PHP requests to FPM. Any path Apache has no file for loads the game, which is how /{code} works: the game reads the 16-letter code from its address and asks the API for that scenario. The editor container is static files behind its own small Apache, reached through the front one at /editor . It holds no data and no secrets; everything it does is a call to /api/editor . Because the game and the editor share an address, they share a sign-in, and the editor's "Test this scene" can open the game on a draft. For development without Docker, npm run dev needs none of this: the game server's file backend reads scenarios/*.json , keeps saves in .data/saves , and answers the few /api calls the client makes. npm run dev:editor runs the editor and the game against apps/api/dev/server.php , a stand-in API that runs the real PHP classes over SQLite. Repository layout Path What it is packages/shared Framework-free TypeScript used by everything: scenario types, normaliser, validator, variable store, condition evaluator, the scene event engine, walkability geometry, the multiplayer world rules and the message protocol. Fully unit-tested. apps/server Colyseus game server. ScenarioRoom is a thin adapter around the shared World ; backend/ hides whether data comes from files or the API. apps/client Phaser client. One data-driven PlayScene plays every scene of every scenario. apps/editor The scenario editor: TypeScript and DOM, no framework. Forms are generated from lists of fields in schema.ts . See apps/editor/README.md . apps/api The Laravel application: the QuestLab tables, seed data for the demo mission, the store the editor and the seeder write through, the compiler that generates scenario JSON from the tables, and the controllers implementing the API contract. scenarios Scenario JSON and media for the file backend. starship.json is generated from the API's seed data ( npm run seed:export ); do not edit it by hand. docs This documentation. docker Dockerfiles for the app, colyseus, editor and apache containers, the app entrypoint and the Apache configuration. tools validate-scenario.ts , make-demo-audio.py . Design decisions One engine, written once. SceneEngine interprets events and actions (ordering, blocking, conditions, overridable, block_hotspots, repeat, run event, cancel, jump with end events) against a small EngineHost interface. The Phaser client implements the host; tests implement a fake with a manual clock. A server-side runner could reuse it if events ever need to be authoritative. One set of world rules, written once. World (movement limits, scene changes, items, shared variables, save data) runs against any object with the right shape. On the server that is the Colyseus room state; in the client's offline mode ( ?offline ) it is plain Maps in the browser. Offline play therefore behaves exactly like online play with one player, which is what an editor preview needs. One room per scenario instance, not per scene. Class-sized groups make this cheap, and it lets shared variables and unique items span scenes without cross-room coordination. If a scenario ever needs hundreds of players in one instance, per-scene filtering with Colyseus state views is the next step. No physics engine. Movement is "feet inside polygons", checked by the same function on client and server. Arcade physics would add a second, slightly different opinion about where a player can be. Screen-space UI in the DOM. Infoboxes, overlays, chat and video are HTML over the canvas: sharp text, real buttons, keyboard and screen-reader access, and no interaction with camera zoom. World-space things (fixed images, spritemaps, labels) are Phaser objects. The runtime reads one compiled document. Scenario content lives in tables that mirror the docs (scenarios, scenes, events, actions, conditions, labels, media, variables, items, characters). ScenarioCompiler generates the JSON from those rows, and publishing stores the result on the scenario. The game only ever reads the published document, so half-finished edits never reach players. One way into the tables. The seeder and the editor both write through ScenarioStore , so seeded content and authored content cannot differ in shape, and both become JSON through the same compiler. The store, the editor's API rules and the compiler are plain PHP with no framework calls, which lets them be tested on SQLite and lets the editor's browser tests run against the real thing. A scenario's address is a code, not a name. Each scenario gets sixteen random lowercase letters when it is created, unique and never changed. Titles and shortnames can be edited freely without breaking a link a teacher has already shared, and codes cannot be guessed by counting. Testing a draft is playing it. The editor does not imitate the game. "Test this scene" opens the real client on the JSON generated from the rows as they are now, offline (the same World rules run in the browser), starting in the chosen scene. What an author sees is what players will get after publishing. Scenes connect through jump actions. A scene edge is a walk-in hotspot spanning one axis whose action is a jump. There is no separate "exit" concept; anything a hotspot or action can do (conditions, sounds, end events) applies to leaving a scene. Client modules Module Responsibility main.ts Sign-in, scenario fetch, avatar choice, connection, boot. net/Api.ts The public API calls. net/Connection.ts OnlineConnection (Colyseus) and OfflineConnection (local World ) behind one interface. core/GameContext.ts What outlives a scene: scenario, variables, flags, music, progress saving. core/SceneRuntime.ts The SceneSystem interface and what a system can see. scenes/PlayScene.ts Creates the event engine and the registered systems for one scene; handles the jump to the next. systems/* One concern each: layers, props, local player, remote players, hotspots, speech, camera, preloading, debug overlay. systems/index.ts is the list. actions/ActionHost.ts The engine's link to Phaser and the UI. actions/presenters/* One presenter per action type; index.ts is the registry. features/* Session-long features: mission checklist, chat, connection status, attachments, progress saving, and stars, XP and the marketplace ( RewardsFeature ). core/Rewards.ts The player's stars, XP, rank and marketplace items as the game knows them; talks to the API for purchases and pretends in a preview. entities/Avatar.ts A player figure with name, speech bubble and attachments. core/assets.ts Media loading, preloading of jump targets, sprite sheets. ui/UiPort.ts , ui/Ui.ts The interface the game uses for on-screen UI, and its HTML implementation. apps/client/README.md explains how to add a system, a presenter or a feature. Adding an action type Add its interface to the Action union in packages/shared/src/types.ts and its name to ACTION_TYPES in scenario.ts . Add its checks to validate.ts . If it is pure logic, handle it in SceneEngine.execute . If it shows or plays something, add it to PresentedAction , write a presenter in apps/client/src/actions/presenters/ and register it in that folder's index.ts . Give it a form: add it to ACTIONS in apps/editor/src/schema.ts , and its name to ScenarioStore::ENUMS . Document it and add a test.

docs.text: Classes, missions and teams A mission is a published scenario. Players find their missions on the page they land on after signing in (the site's front page, / ): a grid with one card per mission. Kind Who sees it Set by Public Everyone, at any time The scenario's setting Who can play it is "Everyone" (the default) Assigned The students a teacher gave it to A teacher, on the editor's Classes page A scenario set to "Only students it is assigned to" is private : it is on nobody's page until its owner assigns it, and nobody else can open its address. A public scenario can be assigned too, for instance to give it a due date or to play it in teams. The setting applies as soon as it is changed; it does not wait for the scenario to be published again. For teachers: the Classes page The editor has two areas, in the bar at the top: Scenarios and Classes . Add your students by the email address they sign in with. A student has to have signed in once before they can be added. A student can be in several teachers' lists. Assign a mission : choose a published scenario, the students it is for, and optionally a due date and a short note. Both are shown on the student's mission card; a due date that has passed is marked. Teams (optional): add teams and put students into them, or use "Share students out evenly". Each team plays in its own copy of the world : the team walks around together, shares what is shared (a boulder one of them knocked down stays down for the whole team, and only for that team), and other teams never appear in it. Without teams, everyone the mission was assigned to shares one copy. Students left in no team share the assignment's own copy. Look in opens a team's copy of the mission as yourself. An assignment can be changed at any time. Teams keep their copy of the world, and their progress, when they are renamed or when students move between them; a student who moves starts in the new team's world with a fresh save there. Instances and save data Every copy of a scenario's world is an instance , named by a group key. The address a player opens carries it: /{code}?group=t7 . Group key Instance public (or none) The one open to everyone a{assignment id} An assignment without teams, or its students who are in no team t{team id} One team Save data belongs to the instance, not to the scenario: What is shared (variables with scope room , where unique items were left) is kept once per instance, in scenario_instances . What is the player's own (their variables, inventory, position, objectives) is kept once per player per instance , in scenario_sessions . A student's team game and the same student's casual game in the public instance are two saves. Stars, XP, rank, the avatar and what was bought in the marketplace belong to the account and are the same everywhere. The game server refuses a player who asks for an instance they do not belong to. A teacher may join any instance of their own assignments, and an admin any instance. Avatars Avatars belong to the platform, not to a scenario: there is one set, and a player keeps the character they chose in every mission. The choice is stored on the account ( users.avatar_media_id ); guests keep theirs in the browser. A player changes character from the missions page, by clicking their character's picture. The set is the avatars table (name, picture, close-up portrait, size, and for a sprite sheet its frames and animations), filled by php artisan qbl:seed from database/seeders/data/avatars.php . There is no screen for editing it yet. When a scenario is served, the set is added to the document as ordinary image media, with ids from 900000 (portraits from 950000), and avatar_media_ids / avatar_portraits are set to match; the editor therefore no longer offers "players can choose this as their avatar". With an empty avatars table a scenario's own avatar_media_ids are used, which is what the standalone file backend does. Tables Table Holds teacher_student Which students a teacher teaches (many to many) assignments A scenario given by a teacher, with due_at and note teams The teams of an assignment assignment_student The students of an assignment and the team each is in, if any avatars The platform's avatars scenario_sessions.group_key Which instance a save belongs to ( public for saves made before instances had their own)

docs.text: Conditions Conditions are placed on events or actions, and describe a global variable-based requirement that must be met before the actions in the event, or the action itself can be executed. If an action, startEvent or endEvent contains a condition that cannot be met, it will be bypassed entirely. If a hotspot contains a condition that cannot be met, looking or clicking within its radius will not trigger, or show any indication the hotspot is active (no hover animation). Primary Attributes Parameter Type Default Description id int condition id event_id int The event id the condition is associated with. type string variable The type of condition. Currently, only “variable” is supported, and this refers to a global variable that has been defined at the scenario level. variable string Either a custom global variable the user has been defined at the scenario level, or any of the reserved variables. operator string One of five operators to perform on the variable, to test if the condition is true or false: =, !=, >, < operand multiple A number (integer or decimal), or a string for which the variable is being evaluated. Variable Operators Operator Description = Test if variable equals variableOperand. If operand is a string, tests are case-insensitive. != Test if variable does not equal operand; If operand is a string, tests are case-insensitive. > Test if variable is greater than operand. If operand is not numeric, the test will always return false. < Test if variable is less than operand. If operand is not numeric, the test will always return false.

docs.text: Events Events are a series of actions that execute in sequential order. There are four types of events: start_events: events that occur when the scene first loads end_events: events that occur immediately before a jump action to another scene hotspots: events that occur when triggered by a hotspot placed at a specific location on the scene indirect_events: events that can only be triggered by a run event action Primary Attributes Parameter Type Default Description id int event id shortname string A unique code identifying the event. scene_id int The scene id the event is associated with. overridable bool false If false, the event cannot be interrupted if another event is initiated. block_hotspots bool false If true, no hotspot can be triggered until this event’s actions are complete. conditions array A list of conditions which must be met before the event can be triggered. actions array A list of actions associated with the event, which sequentially occur when the event is triggered. Hotspots Hotspots contain additional attributes to describe how and when they are triggered. These extra attributes are listed below. Parameter Type Default Description position_x decimal The X coordinate for the hotspot. If null, the entire x-axis is used. position_y decimal The Y coordinate for the hotspot. If null, the entire y-axis is used. radius decimal The radius of the circle around the XY position that can trigger this hotspot. If -1, the hotspot effectively covers the whole screen. If two hotspots overlap, both will be triggered (note that this will invalidate one of them if both are flagged as overridable, so this should be avoided if possible). activate_by_trigger boolean false If true, allow the event to be initiated when a mouse click or screen touch triggers it. The trigger will only work within the radius, unless a radius of -1 is specified. labels array A list of labels which appear along with the hotspot. These can be either text, images, or spritemaps.
